faq.question: Do I need to know how to code?
faq.answer: No. You describe what you want in your own words. You run a few commands to install things, and some plugins are aimed at developers. Each plugin page says who it's for.

faq.question: What does it cost?
faq.answer: The plugins are free and open source under the MIT license. You need your own AI assistant, such as GitHub Copilot or Claude, and a Power Platform environment, which can need Power Platform licenses.

faq.question: How do I update or remove a plugin?
faq.answer: The install-everything command turns on automatic updates. Otherwise, run claude plugin update or copilot plugin update with the plugin name. To remove a plugin, use uninstall instead of update.

faq.question: Where do I get help?
faq.answer: Most plugins include a report-issue skill that drafts a bug report for you. You can also open an issue on GitHub.

transcript.spoken: Your AI assistant knows a lot about code. A plugin teaches it how to build on Power Platform.
transcript.shown: An AI assistant window opens, titled "Your AI assistant". Its Plugins list is empty and reads "No plugins yet", and the message box says "Describe what you need". A Power Pages plugin card flies in and settles into the list.

transcript.spoken: You install a plugin once, and it adds a set of skills.
transcript.shown: Under "Skills in this plugin", five skills unfold from the plugin, each with what it does: /create-site, Start a new site. /edit-site, Change pages. /setup-datamodel, Add tables. /setup-auth, Add sign-in. /deploy-site, Upload the site.

transcript.spoken: Each skill is one job, written down step by step. Creating a Power Pages site is one skill. Deploying it is another.
transcript.shown: /create-site opens into a card titled "Create a Power Pages site" with four steps: Ask what the site is for. Show you a plan to approve. Build the site. Ask before deploying it. A badge reads "One skill, one job". A second card, /deploy-site, titled "Deploy the site", slides in front with three steps: Check your sign-in and environment. Build the site. Upload it to Power Pages.

transcript.spoken: When you describe what you need, your assistant picks the right skill and follows its steps. It asks before it runs commands or changes files.
transcript.shown: The cards fold back into the list of skills, which moves into the window's sidebar. Someone types "Create a Power Pages site for a job board" and sends it. A line links the request to /create-site, and the reply reads "Using /create-site" as three steps get checked off: Asked what the site is for. Showed you a plan to approve. Built the site. Then the assistant stops and asks "Allow this command?" for npm run build, with Deny and Allow buttons and a "Your turn" badge. Allow is pressed and changes to "Allowed".

transcript.spoken: So, plugins are what you install, and skills are the jobs inside them. You just ask.
transcript.shown: The window fades. The plugin card sits on the left above "Plugin: What you install", and the five skills line up on the right above "Skills: The jobs inside it". The film ends on "You just ask." over a message box that says "Describe what you need", with "Power Platform Skills" and microsoft.github.io/power-platform-skills.
